sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fractional CFO Advisory and Multicurrency Ledger Bookkeeping

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA), signed June 29, 2010
Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement (BIPA), signed August 9, 2012

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Taiwan jurisdiction's AML/CFT regime is governed by the Money Laundering Control Act (MLCA), as last comprehensively amended in 2018, the Counter-Terrorism Financing Act, and the Company Act (Article 8) together with the Regulations for the Report of Beneficial Ownership Information by Non-Financial Businesses and Professions (MOEA Order No. 10704604670). The competent authorities are the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) and the Ministry of Justice's investigative authority. UBO declaration and update are made to the Ministry of Economic Affairs central registration system, and access is restricted

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (R.O.C.), Articles 1 through 7, 10, 128 through 135, 172 through 177, 203 through 207, and 387; Foreign Investment Act; Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Residents or Legal Entities; Bookkeepers Act; Certified Public Accountant Act; Business Registration Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs; for a company located in Taipei City, the Taipei City Government Department of Economic Development; all initial filings are made through the MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application for a Company Limited by Shares under Article 387 of the Company Act, accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation, promoter minutes, and capital verification attachments.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an ordinary company limited by shares under the current Company Act. The Board must nonetheless adopt a capital sufficiency statement and deposit the full subscribed capital into a preparatory bank account in Taiwan before registration. For a mainland-area investor, the MOEA Investment Commission may impose a minimum capital amount and a restricted remittance schedule. The subscribed funds are not held in permanent escrow after registration, but may not be withdrawn until the Certificate of Incorporation is issued and, where required, the certified public accountant capital verification report is filed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial authorized share capital of the Company shall be the amount stated in the Articles of Incorporation, divided into ordinary shares with a par value of New Taiwan Dollars 10 per share, and that the subscribers named in the capital subscription schedule hereby subscribe in full for the initial paid-in capital in cash. The Chairperson of the Board is directed to collect all subscription proceeds and to deposit them into an interest-bearing bank account opened in the name of the Company's preparatory office with a licensed bank in Taiwan. No disbursement shall be made until the Company has obtained its Company Registration Certificate and, if applicable, the investment approval from the competent authority has been filed and the paid-in capital has been independently verified by a certified public accountant. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chairperson, together with the General Manager or any other director, is authorized to open, maintain, operate, and close bank accounts in Taiwan and in such other jurisdictions as may be necessary for the Company's business, including operating, tax reserve, payroll, multicurrency settlement, and professional fee accounts. The Chairperson is also authorized to execute bank account opening forms, signatory mandates, online banking terms, and anti-money-laundering questionnaires, provided that any payment exceeding five thousand United States dollars shall require the joint signature of the Chairperson and the General Manager or any two directors. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company in Taiwan shall be located at 12F-3, No. 100, Section 2, Zhongxiao East Road, Zhongzheng District, Taipei City, or at such other lawful address as the Chairperson may determine, and that the Chairperson is authorized to execute the office lease, pay the security deposit, and register the address with the Ministry of Economic Affairs. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons be and hereby are appointed to the statutory offices of the Company: [Name] as Chairperson and chief legal representative; [Name] as General Manager and Managing Director; [Name] as Company Secretary; [Name] as Chief Financial Officer and responsible person for the Company's bookkeeping supervision; and [Name] as the licensed Professional Bookkeeper who shall supervise client bookkeeping, payroll, value-added tax, and tax filing services. Each officer shall hold office until the earlier of removal by the Board or the next annual shareholder meeting, and shall have full authority to execute all contracts, filings, applications, and consents within the scope of his or her office. RESOLVED FURTHER, that any officer or director of the Company is authorized to execute and deliver all registration forms, investment approval applications, tax registration certificates, employer registration notices, bank account documents, and any other instruments necessary to carry out the intent of these resolutions. These resolutions shall remain in full force and effect until the incorporation and statutory licensing of the Company have been completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Investment Commission approval for mainland-area and foreign shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before any Taiwan incorporation step, the foreign investor, including a mainland-China parent, must obtain prior approval for the proposed equity joint venture. Each investing entity must submit notarized certificates of incorporation, audited financial statements for the last fiscal year, a description of the ultimate beneficial ownership chain, and a Taiwan business plan containing the exact ISIC 6920 virtual CFO and bookkeeping service scope. The Investment Commission will assess compliance with the applicable cross-strait investment regulations and may impose conditions on capital contribution, nominee directors, and permitted business scope. The approval letter must be attached to all subsequent filings with the MOEA and the tax administration.
required_dossiers: Notarized certificate of incorporation and articles of association of each shareholder entity
Audited financial statements of each investing shareholder for the last fiscal year
Investment application form filed with the MOEA Investment Commission
Detailed Taiwan business plan for the virtual CFO and bookkeeping services
Notarized board resolution of each shareholder authorizing the investment
Certificate of good standing from the home registry of each shareholder
Power of attorney executed in favor of Taiwan counsel
Passport or national ID copies of shareholders, directors, and the proposed general manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a deficiency notice or query, respond in writing through Taiwan counsel within 30 calendar days with additional evidence of lawful source of funds and the final beneficial ownership chain. If the application is rejected, the proposed shareholding may be restructured through an approved offshore holding vehicle or by reducing the mainland-area participation to a compliant threshold, and a fresh application must be filed with a new reference number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name pre-screening and preparation of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Portal and Commercial Registration Database
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Investment Commission approval, the promoters must select a Chinese corporate name and an optional English translation. The name pre-screening application is filed electronically on the MOEA one-stop portal, and the chosen name must not be identical to any existing Taiwanese company or registered trademark and must not be misleading. Once the name approval certificate is issued, the Articles of Incorporation are drafted in Chinese, including the company name, scope of business limited to ISIC 6920 advisory and bookkeeping services, authorized share capital, directors, registered office seat, and officer provisions. Taiwan counsel must review the draft against the Investment Commission approval to ensure that the business scope is identical and lawful.
required_dossiers: MOEA company name pre-screening application form
Proposed Articles of Incorporation in Chinese with certified English translation
Investment Commission approval letter
Identity documents of all promoters and proposed directors
Three alternative Chinese company names in order of preference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for conflict with an existing company or mark, the portal will display similar names; choose a new alternative name and re-file immediately. A decision on the re-filed name is issued within one business day. If the Articles of Incorporation are found to exceed the approved business scope, revise the Articles to conform to the Investment Commission approval and resubmit before filing the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open preparatory bank account and deposit paid-in capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: An authorized bank in Taiwan, together with a licensed Taiwan certified public accountant for capital verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters register the preparatory office with the local municipal government using the approved company name and then open a temporary capital contribution account with a licensed Taiwanese bank. Each subscriber must wire or deposit the full subscribed share capital into the preparatory account, and the bank issues a capital contribution certificate evidencing the balance. Where the registry or the Investment Commission requires formal verification, the promoters appoint an independent Taiwan certified public accountant to issue a capital verification report. The funds may not be withdrawn until the Company Registration Certificate is issued and, if applicable, the Investment Commission condition on remittance has been satisfied.
required_dossiers: Preparatory office registration form and approval
Investment Commission approval letter
MOEA name pre-approval certificate
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Promoters' board resolution authorizing the capital deposit
Source of funds statement from each subscriber
Bank account opening forms and signatory specimen cards
Passport or national ID copies of authorized account signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank denies account opening due to anti-money-laundering checks, provide a source-of-funds declaration supported by tax returns and audited financial statements, or select another licensed Taiwanese bank. If the capital verification report is challenged, instruct the CPA to re-verify the bank balance certificate within five business days and file a supplementary report with the registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit company registration application to the MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commercial Affairs, through the MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Portal or the Taipei City Government Department of Economic Development counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoter or Taiwan counsel submits the completed company registration package through the MOEA one-stop portal. Every attachment must be in Chinese or accompanied by a certified English translation; documents issued outside Taiwan must be notarized and authenticated by the Taipei Representative Office or equivalent. The registrar performs a legal compliance check against the Company Act, the Articles of Incorporation, the promoter minutes, the bank capital certificate, and the Investment Commission approval. If the application is deficient, the registrar issues a deficiency notice and the applicant has a cure period to amend and resubmit. Upon approval, the MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate and the Unified Business Number.
required_dossiers: Completed Company Registration Application Form under Article 387 of the Company Act
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the promoters' and first shareholder incorporation meeting
Bank capital contribution certificate or certified public accountant capital verification report
Consent forms of directors, supervisors, and statutory officers
Lease agreement and landlord consent for the registered office
MOEA name pre-screening approval
Investment Commission approval letter
Payment proof for the state registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA issues a deficiency notice, the applicant has 30 calendar days to cure; if the Articles of Incorporation are defective, amend them by a valid board resolution and resubmit. If the application is suspended because of unresolved identity or capital questions, engage Taiwan counsel to submit a formal written response with supporting evidence within the cure period; failure to cure results in an automatic dismissal, requiring a new filing and another fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax registration, business licensing, bookkeeper registration, and office safety clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; Taipei City Government Department of Economic Development; Bureau of Labor Insurance; National Health Insurance Administration; Taipei City Fire Department; Ministry of Labor Occupational Safety and Health Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate and Unified Business Number, the Company must register for profit-seeking enterprise income tax, unified invoice issuance, and withholding tax under the Tax Collection Act. The Company must also register as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration. In parallel, the Company must appoint and register a Professional Bookkeeper licensed by the Ministry of Finance to supervise the virtual CFO and bookkeeping business, or, if attestation services are offered, obtain a certified public accountant firm license. The office premises must pass a fire safety inspection and an occupational safety inspection before full operations begin. Failure to complete these post-registration steps will prevent the lawful issuance of tax invoices and the commencement of client billable services.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate from the MOEA
Unified Business Number assignment notice
Tax registration application to the National Taxation Bureau
Application for unified invoice registration
Professional Bookkeeper license certificate and employment contract
Certified public accountant registration if audit or assurance services are provided
Labor and health insurance employer registration forms
Fire safety inspection application with floor plan and occupancy certificate
Occupational safety and health workplace assessment form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Taxation Bureau blocks invoice issuance because a licensed Professional Bookkeeper is not yet on record, hire a duly licensed bookkeeper and submit proof within 10 calendar days. If the fire safety inspection fails, install the required extinguishers, emergency lighting, and exit signage and apply for reinspection within five days. If the occupational safety inspection identifies ergonomic or electrical hazards, file a corrective action plan with the Ministry of Labor and reschedule verification within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau; Taipei City Government Department of Economic Development; no heavy industrial authority applies because the business is a professional service under ISIC 6920.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Professional Bookkeeper Certificate and Tax Practice Registration under the Bookkeepers Act; or Certified Public Accountant Firm License under the Certified Public Accountant Act if attestation services are offered; Business Registration Certificate from the municipal government; Unified Business Number and unified invoice registration from the National Taxation Bureau.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - the undertaking is an office-based professional services business (ISIC 6920) with no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations, and therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - there are no industrial wastewater discharges, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams. Standard office waste must be segregated and collected through approved municipal waste collection channels under the Waste Management Act; zero mandatory industrial discharge limits apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the office premises issued by the Taipei City Fire Department under the Fire Services Act; building occupancy certificate compliance under the Building Act; occupational safety and health inspection under the Occupational Safety and Health Act administered by the Ministry of Labor, covering electrical safety, emergency exit access, and ergonomic workstations. No structural load inspection or chemical hazard clearance is required for an office-only virtual CFO service operation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (Taiwan) - Taxation Administration; regional National Taxation Bureaus; online portal: MOF eTax Portal (etax.nat.gov.tw) for registration and filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. For the onshore JV: apply to the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) for company incorporation and name/business scope approval (one-stop online registration); 2. Upon incorporation, the MOEA Data Center notifies the National Taxation Bureau automatically; the JV must then apply for tax registration within 15 days using the 'Profit-Seeking Enterprise Tax Registration' form at its local National Taxation Bureau, submitting the incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation, identification documents of the directors, and a Taiwan resident agent/manager. 3. The National Taxation Bureau issues an eight-digit Unified Business Identification Number (UBIN), which is the TIN for income tax, Business Tax (VAT), Customs, and Uniform Invoice purposes. 4. For a foreign non-resident enterprise that has no Taiwan fixed place of business but engages in Taiwan-sourced cross-border electronic services, the foreign enterprise must register through the simplified 'Cross-Border Electronic Services Tax Registration' procedure at the National Taxation Bureau; it receives a temporary UBIN and files Business Tax under the cross-border e-commerce regime. 5. All bank accounts, Customs exporter registrations, and Uniform Invoice printing/e-invoice applications require the UBIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is a limited liability profit-seeking enterprise, taxed separately on its taxable income; no pass-through treatment available).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification; Taiwan does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. However, a qualified exporter may apply for monthly Business Tax filing (instead of the standard bi-monthly filing) under Business Tax Act Article 39 to accelerate refunds of zero-rated input VAT.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act (Business Tax; VAT-like indirect tax).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for an incorporated onshore JV; registration is mandatory before commencing business. For a foreign enterprise with no domestic fixed place of business selling electronic services to Taiwan individuals, the threshold is TWD 480,000 in annual sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan operates a Uniform Invoice (UI) system. All VAT-taxable sales require issuance of a Uniform Invoice; electronic Uniform Invoices (e-invoices) must be reported to the MOF E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform through the official Turnkey/API or an approved value-added service center. There is no national real-time fiscal clearance or government digital stamping; anti-fraud controls are implemented through serialized Uniform Invoice numbers, mandatory sequential issuance, duplicate/tamper-evident e-invoice XML/PDF controls, and automated cross-reconciliation with the Business Tax return. Large taxpayers and exporters are expected to use API/machine-to-machine transmission for monthly reconciliation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act to (i) export of goods, (ii) sale of services for use outside Taiwan, and (iii) sales of raw/semi-finished goods to foreign exporters for processing outside Taiwan. For the JV's outsourced virtual CFO services, the supply must be rendered to a foreign buyer, the benefit/use must occur outside Taiwan, the fee must be settled in foreign exchange through a Taiwan bank account, and the services must not be consumed by any Taiwan resident. Goods must physically leave Taiwan customs territory under a valid Export Declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration (Customs Bill of Export) for goods, and a corresponding written zero-rated sales schedule supported by a contract for services
Commercial invoice and service contract/order identifying the foreign purchaser and the scope of the cross-border CFO services
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or international express waybill evidencing physical shipment for goods
Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate (bank inward remittance/banks' certificate of exchange) proving receipt of foreign currency proceeds within the statutory timeline
Packing list and other customs or bank documents (e.g., Shipping Order/Container Number) if requested by Customs Administration or the National Taxation Bureau
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau may review all zero-rated sales with supporting export and foreign-exchange evidence. Where documentation is insufficient or false, the zero rating is reversed and the 5% Business Tax is assessed retrospectively, with overdue interest. Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, administrative penalties may be imposed up to five times the underpaid tax, plus additional penalties for omission of Uniform Invoices or misstatement of taxable sales. The Tax Collection Act assessment period is 5 years in ordinary cases and 7 years in cases of fraud or intentional misdeclaration. Intentional false zero-rating claims may be treated as tax evasion and may trigger criminal referral, while false customs export declarations may additionally be penalized under the Customs Act and Customs Anti-Smuggling Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Full name of the Central Bank or Foreign Exchange Administration
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Analysis of capital vs current account convertibility and profit remittance hurdles
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline and mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating and legal constraints regarding offshore digital EMIs
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Whether directors must appear physically or if remote opening is permitted

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documentation bundle required to satisfy compliance

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific statutory tax holiday for outsourced CFO services in Taiwan. General incentives include a 10% R&D expense tax credit capped at 30% of annual income tax payable under the Statute for Industrial Innovation, and the effective waiver of the 20% levy where taxable income does not exceed NT$120,000. Micro-profit-seeking enterprises may also utilise accelerated depreciation for qualifying software and cloud infrastructure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (Form 15 / 營利事業所得稅結算申報書), e-filed through the Ministry of Finance Tax E-Filing Portal (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim provisional advance payments are required during the fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 5 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year taxpayers must file by 31 May of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from provision of outsourced CFO and bookkeeping services (validate against ISIC 6920 scope).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to non-resident shareholders; this line reflects the Taiwan-resident JV's Taiwan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses directly connected to service income, including salaries and cloud software subscriptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses of foreign shareholder or group allocation are deductible only if supported by the arm's length TP document and actual invoice evidence.
Losses from the Taiwan entity only; no pass-through of foreign owner's losses is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year loss deduction (only losses from the preceding 10 fiscal years for an adequately documented, unbroken enterprise).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign shareholder must not claim the Taiwan JV's NOL on its own home tax return without a foreign tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after applying the 20% statutory rate and tax incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The tax return is a resident entity declaration; foreign shareholders capture their share of profits on their own returns.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under Article 108 of the Income Tax Act, late filing triggers a surcharge of 2% of the tax payable for each month or part of a month of delay, capped at 20%; late payment is additionally penalized under the Tax Collection Act by a surcharge of 1% for every 2 days overdue, capped at 15%, plus daily interest at the postal 1-year deposit rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Related-Party Transaction and Transfer Pricing Disclosure Schedules (Annexes to Form 15), e-submitted with the annual return through the integrated tax return system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed with the annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return within 5 months after fiscal year-end; the contemporaneous Transfer Pricing Report must be prepared by the return due date and made available on tax authority demand.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party counterparty identification and country of tax residence (including PRC shareholder status).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a CN/TW JV, the PRC shareholder must be identified as a related party but without treaty-resident relief because no effective cross-strait DTA is in place.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Type and amount of controlled transactions — management fees, software licences, intercompany service charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany service fees should be charged at cost plus arm's-length margin; payments to foreign shareholder are subject to Taiwan WHT unless a specific exemption is confirmed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing methodology selection and comparability adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no local comparables, TNMM is commonly used for CFO outsourcing activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or submit TP documentation when required can trigger an upward TP adjustment and a fine under Income Tax Act Art. 110; Class A/B reporting defects may invite additional surcharges of up to 3× understated tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Non-Resident Withholding Tax Remittance and Withholding Certificate Return (Form 30 / 扣繳憑單申報), e-submitted through the Tax E-Filing Portal or delivered to the district tax bureau
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: At each remittance/payout; a consolidated annual filing of withholding certificates by the end of January following the payout year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Withhold at the time of payout; payover within 10 days after the payment date; annual withholding certificate filing by 31 January of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross proceeds of dividend distribution and 21% WHT due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The China-resident shareholder cannot obtain a statutory rate reduction absent effective DTA; if any specific DTA applies, attach TRC before the remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest paid to non-resident lender and 15% WHT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident lender must provide an ownership breakdown and accept the arm's-length interest determination; excess interest may be treated as dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Royalties / unrecaptured technical service fees and 20% WHT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To claim treaty royalty relief (e.g., 10%), submit a valid TRC and beneficial ownership statement to the payor before withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Short-withholding penalty of 15% of the shortfall may be imposed on the payor; the uncollected tax itself remains collectible from the non-resident; if the payor deliberately evades withholding, criminal tax evasion liabilities under Tax Collection Act Art. 42 can apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% statutory withholding on dividend payouts to non-resident corporate shareholders not operating as a fixed place of business in Taiwan (Income Tax Act Art. 88).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since the PRC and Taiwan have no ratified Double Taxation Agreement (the 2015 Cross-Strait Tax Agreement has not entered into force), no DTA dividend reduction currently exists for the PRC shareholder. Should a qualifying treaty (e.g., Japan, Singapore, UK) apply, the foreign shareholder must deliver a valid Tax Residence Certificate, a Form of Treaty Address/Beneficial Ownership declaration, and a written request to the Taiwan tax officer before the dividend payment date; after approval, the issuer withholds at the treaty rate, and the foreign shareholder may still credit the tax in its home jurisdiction. Where no DTA applies, unilateral foreign tax credit or unilateral relief under Taiwan Income Tax Act may only allow a credit abroad, not reduce Taiwan WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 20% for royalty/technical-know-how fees and 15% for debt interest paid to non-residents. Under Taiwan's DTAs, rates are commonly reduced to 10% (royalties and interest) if the beneficial owner is a resident of the treaty country; fees for management services rendered to a foreign parent do not escape WHT unless the source is determined offshore by substance analysis. Related-party interest beyond the permissible 3:1 debt-equity ratio is recharacterized as dividends and subject to 21% withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A contemporaneous Local File/Transfer Pricing Report is required where annual related-party controlled transactions exceed NT$50 million (~USD 1.6 million). A group Master File is required when the ultimate parent group's worldwide consolidated revenue exceeds NT$1.5 billion; even where the NT$50 million threshold is not met, any related-party dealings above NT$5 million must be reported in the related-party breakdown and supported by minimal fact documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not issue BVI/Cayman-style ESR notifications; instead, the tax authority applies an anti-abuse 'real economic operation' doctrine under Income Tax Act Art. 43-3/43-4 and the general anti-abuse principle of IAT Art. 12-1. A Taiwan JV without local offices, substantive payroll, or a demonstrable head office is at risk of being disregarded for treaty/income-sourcing purposes, of having its intercompany payments disallowed, or of being characterized as an agent/PE of the foreign shareholder.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-reporting of virtual CFO service fees (e.g., Stripe and Wise collections directed to foreign banks), creating fictitious cost deductions, or issuing cash-invoice schemes to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil: underpaid tax, interest, plus a penalty equal to 1-3 times the understated tax under Income Tax Act Art. 110. Criminal: Tax Collection Act Art. 41 — imprisonment up to 5 years, detention, and/or a fine up to NT$60,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Taiwan Company Act Art. 154(2) permits veil-piercing for abuse of corporate personality; directors and de facto managers are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax fine; tax authorities may impose an order prohibiting departure from Taiwan under Tax Collection Act Art. 24 when tax arrears exceed NT$1 million.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a tax-resident Taiwan JV with no substantive office, a single nominee director, a mailbox seat, and routing revenue through low-tax jurisdictions without commercial rationale.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the company's losses and a reallocation of income under IAT Art. 43-3 and Art. 43-4 for circular transactions; added penalty of up to 3× the tax avoided under Art. 110; administrative dissolution possible under the Company Act if the company is deemed inactive.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may disregard the JV's separate legal existence under Company Act Art. 154(2); directors liable for corporate debts, withholding taxes, and repatriation of assets; travel bans are imposed on directors with large tax/debt exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting and executing client fund transfers through Stripe Billing and Wise without collecting KYC/beneficial-ownership data, and deliberately omitting suspicious cross-border transfers to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money Laundering Control Act — fines from NT$500,000 to NT$5 million and possible suspension of license; criminally, up to 7 years' imprisonment and fines if the company laundered >NT$10 million.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are natural persons under the AML/CFT legal matrix; they face criminal prosecution, confiscation of gains, restrictions on leaving Taiwan, and disqualification from serving as directors under the Financial Supervisory Commission enforcement orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold / Repatriation in Wrong Form (Dividend WHT/Thin Cap)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing profits to the PRC shareholder as 'loan' or 'management fee' to avoid 21% dividend withholding, or allowing the TW entity to be thinly capitalized by an intra-group loan at a non-arm's length interest rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Increases tax: recharacterization of payments as dividends under IAT Arts. 43-1/43-2; the payer is held liable for the short-collected WHT plus a 15% penalty under Art. 114, in addition to the 21% tax on dividend and 20% tax on the disguised fee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: When the director intentionally authorized mischaracterized payments, personal liability attaches to the unpaid withholding taxes. Travel restrictions are effective to secure tax payment; directors may face criminal charges if fraudulent avoidance is established.
